name: Standard Residual
tagline: Every sublayer adds its output to one unscaled stream. The control for HC, mHC and Block AttnRes.
description: The Dense Baseline's 23 full-attention layers at FFN 6144, with nanochat's learned residual and x0 coefficients and backout replaced by the plain Pre-Norm update h + F(RMSNorm(h)) around every attention and FFN sublayer. Value embeddings, smear, embeddings and the ReLU² FFN are unchanged. The 47 native residual scalars stay registered, frozen and unused, so its parameter count equals Dense. Calibrated independently to +0.041% of the shared budget; HC, mHC and Block AttnRes are reported as paired differences from this run.
paperTitle: Identity Mappings in Deep Residual Networks
mechanism: h ← h + F(RMSNorm(h)) around each of the 46 attention and FFN sublayers
No learned residual or x0 coefficients and no backout; those 47 scalars stay frozen and unused
Dense's shell otherwise: 23 full-attention layers, 12 heads of 128, FFN 6144, value embeddings
limitations: Single seed 42 on 8 × A800. The preregistered pilot was skipped by the owner's decision; the formal run started from random initialization. It differs from the Dense Baseline only in the residual path, so the pair separates nanochat's learned residual scalars from plain Pre-Norm addition. Parameters, memory and speed are outcomes, not controls.
